summary: James H. Austin works in Buddhist studies and other fields, having studied under Nanrei Kobori, Joshu Sasaki, and Katsujo Terayama. He held posts at the universities of Oregon, Colorado, Missouri, and Idaho, alongside several sabbatical appointments.

James Hadley was a linguist who studied at Yale College (~1840–1842) and under Edward Elbridge Salisbury in 1849. He held academic posts at Middlebury College (1844–1845) and Yale University (1845–1872).

James Haughton Woods studied at Harvard, Strasbourg, and under Paul Deussen, Charles Rockwell Lanman, Arthur Venis, and Mukunda Shastri Adkar. Specializing in Indology and philosophy, he held a post at Harvard University in 1914.

A scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics, Manatt studied at Grinnell and Yale, the latter under William Dwight Whitney. He held posts at Denison, Marietta, the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, and Brown University (Professor, ~1892–1915).
James Ishmael Ford is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Pacific School of Religion and trained under Houn Jiyu-Kennett and John Tarrant. He also founded Boundless Way Zen.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Powell earned degrees from Northwestern, Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD, 1998). He studied under David Tracy, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

James L. Fitzgerald is an Indologist who served as Professor at the University of Tennessee (attested 2004–2006) and as Das Professor of Sanskrit in the Department of Classics at Brown University (attested 2019).

James Mallinson is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Eton and Oxford, completing his D.Phil. under Alexis Sanderson. In 2013, he became Lecturer in Sanskrit and Classical Indian Studies at SOAS University of London.

James Mark Shields is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 2016, he was attested as Associate Professor at Bucknell University and as an Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
James Matthew Baskind works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Yale University under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein (attested 2006).

James McHugh studied at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard (PhD), working under Lawrence McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil. An Indologist and religious studies scholar, he has held posts at Cornell and the University of Southern California.

James Miller specializes in sinology and religious studies. He completed an MA at the University of Cambridge and a PhD at Boston University, and was attested in 2014 as Professor of Chinese Studies and Religious Studies at Queen's University Belfast.
James Montgomery studied at the University of Glasgow (~1980–1990). In 1997, he held a post at the Faculty of Asian and Middle Eastern Studies at the University of Cambridge.
James Morison was an Indologist who studied under Georg Bühler as a Specialschüler. He served as Librarian at the University of Oxford (attested 1917–1920).

James Prinsep was a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served at the India Government Mint in Kolkata beginning in 1819 and was a member of the Asiatic Society from 1832 to 1838, succeeding Horace Hayman Wilson.

An Indology and philosophy scholar, Ballantyne studied at Edinburgh under James Michael and Francis Johnson. He taught at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy, served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and was librarian at the India Office Library.
James Rennell was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the East India Company from 1762 to 1777 and in the Bengal Engineers beginning in 1764.

James Robson is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts as Assistant Professor at the University of Michigan (attested 2006–2014) and Associate Professor at Harvard University (~2008).

An Indology and history/archaeology scholar, Cotton was educated at Magdalen College School, Brighton College, Winchester College, and Trinity College, Oxford. He held a post at Queens' College, Cambridge, from 1871 to 1874.

James Tod worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served with the East India Company from ~1798 to 1822 and was Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from ~1823 to 1835.
